reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a cryptocurrency arbitrage method as an easy, repeatable 15% return in 10 minutes and directs viewers to purchase about $1,000 in crypto, transfer BNB between platforms, and exchange it for USDT. It also directs viewers toward a paid VIP channel, making the rapid-profit claim part of a concrete solicitation. The video includes a warning about scammers, and the records do not verify the platforms, prices, balances, transaction outcomes, or unclear password-sharing instruction.

citations.quote: In this video I will show you how easy it is to earn 15% profit on crypto arbitrage in 10 minutes.
You can use this strategy an unlimited number of times.
Links from the video: Exchange: https://binance.com Exchanger: :https://bymirc.com/
make sure that BNB is more expensive there than on Binance. Right now, the difference is almost 15%. And this is the market spread, in other words, our earnings.
Select Market and specify the amount of USDT. As an example, purchase $1000.

opening.argument: The presentation includes an explicit anti-scam warning: viewers are told to contact the administrator first and “be aware of scammers.” That warning is inconsistent with presenting every linked opportunity as automatically trustworthy. The narration also identifies a concrete withdrawal constraint, stating that the daily withdrawal limit is $50,000. These cautions place the discussion in a risk-aware context, while the material itself does not state that returns are guaranteed or that viewers must surrender funds to the presenter. The appropriate reading is therefore an educational warning about navigating crypto transactions, not deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: Contact our administrator first, so be aware of scammers.
But remember the daily withdrawal limit is $50,000!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument treats the advertised percentage and the $1,000 example as proof of deception, but those quotations establish only what the video discusses, not that the result is guaranteed or fabricated. The warning about scammers is not irrelevant: it directly cautions viewers in the same narration. The records also do not establish that any linked service is controlled by the creator or that viewers were asked to transfer money to him.

citations.quote: In this video I will show you how easy it is to earn 15% profit on crypto arbitrage in 10 minutes.
Contact our administrator first, so be aware of scammers.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning is brief and does not qualify the central promise. The description still calls earning 15% in 10 minutes easy and says the strategy can be used an unlimited number of times. The narration then presents “almost 15%” as earnings and reports a $150 profit, so the caution does not convert the rapid-return promotion into neutral scam awareness.

opening.argument: The material is structured as an operational walkthrough. The narration gives sequential instructions for selecting a BNB-USDT spot pair, buying an example amount, depositing BNB, exchanging it for USDT, and withdrawing the result. The supplied frames likewise show trading, deposit, withdrawal, exchange, and transaction-history screens. That evidence supports reading the video as a demonstration of an arbitrage workflow rather than a demand that viewers pay the presenter. A tutorial can explain a claimed method without certifying that every future trade will produce the same outcome.

citations.quote: Go to Trade, and select the Spot section. Search and select BNB-USDT as a trading pair.
Now let's exchange BNB and USDT the exchange commission is 0.1%.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the content a tutorial does not answer what the tutorial teaches. It expressly combines a rapid percentage claim with instructions to purchase $1,000 of crypto and move it to another exchanger. The VIP-channel invitation also gives the demonstration a promotional purpose. A step-by-step format can make a misleading financial promise more actionable; it does not neutralize that promise.

citations.quote: As an example, purchase $1000.
If you still have questions or have a desire to purchase a subscription to the VIP channel
In this video I will show you how easy it is to earn 15% profit on crypto arbitrage in 10 minutes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The workflow is not merely abstract education: it tells viewers to buy BNB, transfer it between platforms, and withdraw USDT. The description frames the method as easy, repeatable profit, while the narration says the spread is earnings. Screens showing interfaces do not independently verify the prices, balances, or claimed outcome, so the tutorial framing does not cure the unsupported return claim.

citations.quote: You can use this strategy an unlimited number of times.
The withdrawal is successful and will take five to eight minutes.
Right now, the difference is almost 15%.

opening.argument: The described activity is an ordinary exchange transaction: acquire one cryptocurrency, transfer it to an exchange service, convert it to another cryptocurrency, and withdraw the proceeds. The narration identifies a 0.1% exchange commission and instructs the viewer to use matching networks, which are normal operational details of a service transaction. The supplied material does not show a request to pay the presenter, recruit a downline, or provide credentials to the creator. It also does not establish that the external platforms are safe, so this reading treats them as services without certifying them.

citations.quote: the exchange commission is 0.1%.
It is important that the networks we choose are the same on Binance and Birmark.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary-transaction framing omits the central inducement: the video describes 15% profit in 10 minutes and unlimited repetition. The $1,000 purchase and transfer sequence is not just a neutral service description when it is paired with that return claim. The existence of a commission or matching networks explains mechanics, but does not substantiate the advertised spread or reported profit.

citations.quote: In this video I will show you how easy it is to earn 15% profit on crypto arbitrage in 10 minutes.
As an example, purchase $1000.
the exchange commission is 0.1%.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing scam mechanism does not resolve the explicit profit promotion. The content directs viewers to named exchange destinations, offers a VIP subscription for additional strategies, and presents an alleged $150 result after the transfer sequence. The records show interfaces and narration, but they do not independently prove that the platforms, spread, balances, or outcome are genuine, making the ordinary-commerce analogy insufficient.
